summary: Anne C. Klein is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies and Tibetology. She studied at Binghamton, Wisconsin-Madison, and Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins and several traditional teachers. She held posts at Harvard Divinity School, Rice University, and the Dawn Mountain Center.

Anne Casile is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. She studied under Claudine Bautze-Picron and held posts as an AHRC research assistant at the British Museum (~2008–2010) and at the French National Research Institute for Sustainable Development (~2011).

Anne E. Monius was a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She earned her degrees at Harvard under Diana L. Eck and Kausalya Hart. She taught at the University of Virginia (1997–2002) and Harvard University (~2001–2019).

Anne Feldhaus is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. She studied at Manhattanville College (~1967–1971) and completed her doctoral degree at the University of Pennsylvania (~1971–1976), later serving as a Distinguished Foundation Professor of Religious Studies at Arizona State University (1981).

Anne Hardgrove is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. She studied at Carleton College (~1986–1990) and the University of Michigan (~1992–1999), and held a post at the University of Texas at San Antonio in 2000.

Anne M. Blackburn works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies. A graduate student at the University of Chicago (1991), she served as Assistant Professor of Religion at Cornell University (~2001–2024) and became a professor at Harvard University (~2024).

Anne MacDonald specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. She studied at the University of British Columbia under Shotaro Iida, Ashok Narhar Aklujkar, and Geshe Tashi Namgyal, and under Lambert Schmithausen and Karin Preisendanz, later holding posts at the University of Vienna.

Anne Nishimura Morse specializes in Japanology, history, and archaeology. She studied under John M. Rosenfield, Taka Yanagisawa, and Yutaka Hirata. She held posts at Smith College, Tokyo National Research Institute for Cultural Properties, Nara National Museum, and Kyoto National Museum.

Anne Ruth Hansen specializes in Buddhist studies, history, and religious studies. Having studied under Charles Hallisey, she held positions at the University of Wisconsin–Milwaukee (attested 2007) and the University of Wisconsin–Madison (attested 2012–2026).
Anne-Marie Blondeau is a Tibetologist who studied under Rolf Alfred Stein and held a post at the École Pratique des Hautes Études.
Annegret Bollée was a linguist who pursued her studies at the University of Hamburg (~1956–1961), Aix-Marseille University (~1960–1961), and the University of Bonn (1969).

Annemarie Schimmel worked in religious studies, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. She studied at Berlin and Marburg under Hans Heinrich Schaeder and Friedrich Heiler, later holding professorships at Marburg, Ankara University (1954–1967), and Harvard University (1967–1992).

Annemarie von Gabain was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and history. She studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1923–1929), where she held a post (~1938–1946), before serving as a professor at the University of Hamburg (~1950–1966).

Annette Baier was a philosopher who studied at the University of Otago (~1948–1952) and earned her PhD at Somerville College (1952). She taught at Carnegie Mellon University (~1968–1973) and the University of Pittsburgh's philosophy department (~1973–1995).

Annette L. Heitmann specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and the University of Vienna, where she earned her doctorate in 2002, studying under Christian Lindtner and David Seyfort Ruegg.

Annette Schmiedchen is an Indologist and historian. She earned her PhD at Humboldt University of Berlin and completed her Habilitation at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg, later holding posts at Halle-Wittenberg (~1995–2014) and Humboldt University (~2014).

Annie Besant was an Indologist and religious studies figure who studied at Birkbeck, University of London (~1879–1883). She served as President of the Theosophical Society (~1907–1933) and founded Banaras Hindu University in 1898, later serving as its president (~1916).

Anthony C. Yu was a scholar of Sinology and religious studies. Educated at Houghton University, Fuller Theological Seminary, and the University of Chicago (PhD ~1963–1969), he was a distinguished professor of humanities and religion and literature at the University of Chicago (~1968–2005).

Anthony Cerulli specializes in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Chicago (~2000–2007) and held posts as Professor of South Asian Studies and Director of Graduate Studies at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~2014).

Anthony François Paulus Hulsewé was a Sinologist and historian. He studied at Leiden University under J. J. L. Duyvendak (1928), where he later served as a lecturer in Chinese (1946) and professor (1956–1975).
